sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvaitad ākhyānavaraṃ dharmarāḍ janamejaya bhrātaraś cāsya te sarve nārāyaṇaparābhavan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this most excellent narrative, O Janamejaya, the king of righteousness and all his brothers became wholly devoted to Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: jitaṃ bhagavatā tena puruṣeṇeti bhārata nityaṃ japyaparā bhūtvā sarasvatīm udīrayan
english: Saying "Victory belongs to that blessed Person," O Bhārata, they became ever intent on silent recitation, lifting up their voices to Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: yo hy asmākaṃ guruḥ śreṣṭhaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano muniḥ sa jagau paramaṃ japyaṃ nārāyaṇam udīrayan
english: He who is our most excellent teacher, the sage Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, himself chanted that supreme litany, sounding forth the name of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: gatvāntarikṣāt satataṃ kṣīrodam amṛtāśayam pūjayitvā ca deveśaṃ punar āyāt svam āśramam
english: Passing ever through the sky to the Ocean of Milk, that abode of nectar, and having worshipped the Lord of the gods, he would return again to his own hermitage.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathaṃ sa bhagavān devo yajñeṣv agraharaḥ prabhuḥ yajñadhārī ca satataṃ vedavedāṅgavit tathā
english: Janamejaya said: How is it that this blessed Lord, the god who is foremost receiver of offerings at sacrifices, who upholds the sacrifice and forever knows the Vedas and their ancillary sciences—

sanskrit: nivṛttaṃ cāsthito dharmaṃ kṣemī bhāgavatapriyaḥ pravṛttidharmān vidadhe sa eva bhagavān prabhuḥ
english: —how is it that this same blessed Lord, secure in peace and dear to His devotees, though established in the dharma of withdrawal, yet ordained the dharmas of active engagement?

sanskrit: kathaṃ pravṛttidharmeṣu bhāgārhā devatāḥ kṛtāḥ kathaṃ nivṛttidharmāś ca kṛtā vyāvṛttabuddhayaḥ
english: How were the deities, worthy of a share of offerings, made for the dharmas of engagement, and how were the followers of the dharma of withdrawal made, their minds turned away from the world?

sanskrit: etaṃ naḥ saṃśayaṃ vipra chindhi guhyaṃ sanātanam tvayā nārāyaṇakathā śrutā vai dharmasaṃhitā
english: Cut away this doubt of ours, O brahmin—this eternal mystery—for by you the tale of Nārāyaṇa, that compendium of dharma, has been heard.

sanskrit: ime sabrahmakā lokāḥ sasurāsuramānavāḥ kriyāsv abhyudayoktāsu saktā dṛśyanti sarvaśaḥ mokṣaś coktas tvayā brahman nirvāṇaṃ paramaṃ sukham
english: These worlds, together with Brahmā, with gods and demons and men, are seen everywhere bound to ritual acts that are said to yield prosperity; and yet liberation too has been declared by you, O brahmin—extinction, the supreme bliss.

sanskrit: ye ca muktā bhavantīha puṇyapāpavivarjitāḥ te sahasrārciṣaṃ devaṃ praviśantīti śuśrumaḥ
english: And those who become liberated here, freed from merit and sin—we have heard that they enter into the god of a thousand rays.

sanskrit: aho hi duranuṣṭheyo mokṣadharmaḥ sanātanaḥ yaṃ hitvā devatāḥ sarvā havyakavyabhujo 'bhavan
english: Ah, how hard to follow is the eternal dharma of liberation—forsaking which all the deities became eaters of the oblations offered to gods and to the ancestors!

sanskrit: kiṃ nu brahmā ca rudraś ca śakraś ca balabhit prabhuḥ sūryas tārādhipo vāyur agnir varuṇa eva ca ākāśaṃ jagatī caiva ye ca śeṣā divaukasaḥ
english: What then of Brahmā and Rudra, and the lord Śakra who shattered Bala, of Sūrya, the Moon who is lord of stars, of Vāyu, Agni, and Varuṇa, of Space and Earth, and all the remaining dwellers of heaven?

sanskrit: pralayaṃ na vijānanti ātmanaḥ parinirmitam tatas te nāsthitā mārgaṃ dhruvam akṣayam avyayam
english: They do not perceive the dissolution that has been fashioned for their own selves; and so they have not entered upon the path that is fixed, imperishable, and unchanging.

sanskrit: smṛtvā kālaparīmāṇaṃ pravṛttiṃ ye samāsthitāḥ doṣaḥ kālaparīmāṇe mahān eṣa kriyāvatām
english: Recalling the measure of time, they who have taken their stand on active engagement—this is the great flaw, bound up with the measure of time, that besets those given to ritual works.

sanskrit: etan me saṃśayaṃ vipra hṛdi śalyam ivārpitam chindhītihāsakathanāt paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: Cut away this doubt of mine, O brahmin, that is lodged like a barb in my heart; great is my longing to hear the telling of this ancient lore.

sanskrit: kathaṃ bhāgaharāḥ proktā devatāḥ kratuṣu dvija kimarthaṃ cādhvare brahmann ijyante tridivaukasaḥ
english: How is it, O twice-born, that the deities are declared receivers of a share at sacrifices, and to what end, O brahmin, are the dwellers of the triple heaven worshipped at the rite?

sanskrit: ye ca bhāgaṃ pragṛhṇanti yajñeṣu dvijasattama te yajanto mahāyajñaiḥ kasya bhāgaṃ dadanti vai
english: And those who receive a share at the sacrifices, O best of the twice-born—when they themselves sacrifice with great offerings, to whom do they give a share?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca aho gūḍhatamaḥ praśnas tvayā pṛṣṭo janeśvara nātaptatapasā hy eṣa nāvedaviduṣā tathā nāpurāṇavidā cāpi śakyo vyāhartum añjasā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Ah, a most hidden question you have asked, O lord of men! For one who has not practiced austerity, who does not know the Veda, who is not versed in the ancient lore—by such a one it cannot readily be expounded.

sanskrit: hanta te kathayiṣyāmi yan me pṛṣṭaḥ purā guruḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano vyāso vedavyāso mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: Come then, I shall tell you that which long ago my teacher was asked—Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana Vyāsa, the great sage, the arranger of the Vedas.

sanskrit: sumantur jaiminiś caiva pailaś ca sudṛḍhavrataḥ ahaṃ caturthaḥ śiṣyo vai pañcamaś ca śukaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Sumantu and Jaimini, and Paila of firm vows, I myself the fourth pupil, and Śuka counted the fifth—

sanskrit: etān samāgatān sarvān pañca śiṣyān damānvitān śaucācārasamāyuktāñ jitakrodhāñ jitendriyān
english: these five pupils all assembled together, endowed with self-restraint, joined to purity of conduct, masters of their anger and of their senses—

sanskrit: vedān adhyāpayām āsa mahābhāratapañcamān merau girivare ramye siddhacāraṇasevite
english: to these he taught the Vedas, with the Mahābhārata as a fifth, upon Meru, that lovely chief of mountains, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: teṣām abhyasyatāṃ vedān kadā cit saṃśayo 'bhavat eṣa vai yas tvayā pṛṣṭas tena teṣāṃ prakīrtitaḥ tataḥ śruto mayā cāpi tavākhyeyo 'dya bhārata
english: As they were reciting the Vedas, a doubt once arose among them—the very one that you have asked—and by him it was proclaimed to them; thus it was heard by me as well, and today, O Bhārata, it is to be told to you.

sanskrit: śiṣyāṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā sarvājñānatamonudaḥ parāśarasutaḥ śrīmān vyāso vākyam uvāca ha
english: Having heard the words of his pupils, the dispeller of all the darkness of ignorance, the illustrious son of Parāśara, Vyāsa, spoke these words:

sanskrit: mayā hi sumahat taptaṃ tapaḥ paramadāruṇam bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyac ca jānīyām iti sattamāḥ
english: "By me has been practiced a very great and most severe austerity, that I might know what has been, what is, and what shall be, O most excellent ones.

sanskrit: tasya me taptatapaso nigṛhītendriyasya ca nārāyaṇaprasādena kṣīrodasyānukūlataḥ
english: And for me, who had practiced austerity and held my senses in check, by the grace of Nārāyaṇa, on the favoring shore of the Ocean of Milk—

sanskrit: traikālikam idaṃ jñānaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ yathepsitam tac chṛṇudhvaṃ yathājñānaṃ vakṣye saṃśayam uttamam yathā vṛttaṃ hi kalpādau dṛṣṭaṃ me jñānacakṣuṣā
english: —this knowledge of the three times arose, even as I desired. Hear it: according to my knowledge I shall expound this supreme doubt, just as it came to pass at the beginning of the aeon, seen by me with the eye of wisdom.

sanskrit: paramātmeti yaṃ prāhuḥ sāṃkhyayogavido janāḥ mahāpuruṣasaṃjñāṃ sa labhate svena karmaṇā
english: That which the knowers of Sāṃkhya and Yoga call the Supreme Self attains, by its own action, the appellation of the Great Person.

sanskrit: tasmāt prasūtam avyaktaṃ pradhānaṃ tad vidur budhāḥ avyaktād vyaktam utpannaṃ lokasṛṣṭyartham īśvarāt
english: From that the Unmanifest is brought forth—the wise know it as the Primal Matter; and from the Unmanifest, from the Lord, the manifest arose, for the sake of the creation of the worlds.

sanskrit: aniruddho hi lokeṣu mahān ātmeti kathyate yo 'sau vyaktatvam āpanno nirmame ca pitāmaham so 'haṃkāra iti proktaḥ sarvatejomayo hi saḥ
english: Aniruddha is spoken of in the worlds as the Great Self; and he who, having come into manifestation, fashioned the Grandfather—he is called the principle of I-ness, for he is wholly made of radiance.

sanskrit: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam ahaṃkāraprasūtāni mahābhūtāni bhārata
english: Earth, wind, space, water, and light as the fifth—these great elements are born of the principle of I-ness, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: mahābhūtāni sṛṣṭvātha tadguṇān nirmame punaḥ bhūtebhyaś caiva niṣpannā mūrtimanto 'ṣṭa tāñ śṛṇu
english: Having created the great elements, He then fashioned their qualities anew; and from the elements there came forth eight embodied beings—hear of them.

sanskrit: marīcir aṅgirāś cātriḥ pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ vasiṣṭhaś ca mahātmā vai manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvas tathā jñeyāḥ prakṛtayo 'ṣṭau tā yāsu lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: Marīci, Aṅgiras, and Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, and Manu the self-born—these are to be known as the eight primal natures upon which the worlds are established.

sanskrit: vedān vedāṅgasaṃyuktān yajñān yajñāṅgasaṃyutān nirmame lokasiddhyarthaṃ brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ aṣṭābhyaḥ prakṛtibhyaś ca jātaṃ viśvam idaṃ jagat
english: The Vedas joined with their ancillary sciences, and the sacrifices joined with their constituent parts, Brahmā the Grandfather of the worlds fashioned for the world's accomplishment; and from these eight primal natures was born this whole universe.

sanskrit: rudro roṣātmako jāto daśānyān so 'sṛjat svayam ekādaśaite rudrās tu vikārāḥ puruṣāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: Rudra, whose very nature is wrath, was born, and he himself created ten others; these eleven Rudras are remembered as the modifications, the personal forms.

sanskrit: te rudrāḥ prakṛtiś caiva sarve caiva surarṣayaḥ utpannā lokasiddhyarthaṃ brahmāṇaṃ samupasthitāḥ
english: Those Rudras, and the primal nature, and all the divine seers, having arisen for the world's accomplishment, drew near to Brahmā.

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi sṛṣṭā bhagavaṃs tvayā vai prabhaviṣṇunā yena yasminn adhīkāre vartitavyaṃ pitāmaha
english: "We have indeed been created by you, O blessed and almighty Lord; tell us, O Grandfather, by whom and in what office each is to act.

sanskrit: yo 'sau tvayā vinirdiṣṭo adhikāro 'rthacintakaḥ paripālyaḥ kathaṃ tena so 'dhikāro 'dhikāriṇā
english: That charge which has been assigned by you, fixed upon its purpose—how is that charge to be carried out and upheld by the one charged with it?

sanskrit: pradiśasva balaṃ tasya yo 'dhikārārthacintakaḥ evam ukto mahādevo devāṃs tān idam abravīt
english: Grant the power befitting each one who is charged with his appointed task." So addressed, the Great God spoke thus to those gods:

sanskrit: sādhv ahaṃ jñāpito devā yuṣmābhir bhadram astu vaḥ mamāpy eṣā samutpannā cintā yā bhavatāṃ matā
english: "Well have I been reminded by you, O gods—may good befall you! This very concern that is in your minds has arisen in mine as well.

sanskrit: lokatantrasya kṛtsnasya kathaṃ kāryaḥ parigrahaḥ kathaṃ balakṣayo na syād yuṣmākaṃ hy ātmanaś ca me
english: How shall the management of the whole framework of the worlds be undertaken? How may there be no waning of strength—neither yours nor my own?

sanskrit: itaḥ sarve 'pi gacchāmaḥ śaraṇaṃ lokasākṣiṇam mahāpuruṣam avyaktaṃ sa no vakṣyati yad dhitam
english: From here let us all go for refuge to the Witness of the worlds, the Great Person, the Unmanifest; He will tell us what is for our good."

sanskrit: tatas te brahmaṇā sārdham ṛṣayo vibudhās tathā kṣīrodasyottaraṃ kūlaṃ jagmur lokahitārthinaḥ
english: Then those seers and gods, together with Brahmā, went to the northern shore of the Ocean of Milk, seeking the welfare of the worlds.

sanskrit: te tapaḥ samupātiṣṭhan brahmoktaṃ vedakalpitam sa mahāniyamo nāma tapaścaryā sudāruṇā
english: There they undertook the austerity declared by Brahmā and ordained by the Veda—that very severe practice of penance named the Great Observance.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ dṛṣṭir bāhavaś ca ekāgraṃ ca mano 'bhavat ekapādasthitāḥ samyak kāṣṭhabhūtāḥ samāhitāḥ
english: Their gaze upraised and their arms uplifted, their minds became one-pointed; standing each upon a single foot, motionless as wood, they were wholly collected.

sanskrit: divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ te tapas taptvā tad uttamam śuśruvur madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ vedavedāṅgabhūṣitām
english: For a thousand divine years having practiced that supreme austerity, they heard a sweet voice, adorned with the Vedas and their ancillary sciences:

sanskrit: bho bhoḥ sabrahmakā devā ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ svāgatenārcya vaḥ sarvāñ śrāvaye vākyam uttamam
english: "Hail, hail, O gods together with Brahmā, and you seers rich in austerity! Honoring you all with welcome, I cause a supreme utterance to be heard by you.

sanskrit: vijñātaṃ vo mayā kāryaṃ tac ca lokahitaṃ mahat pravṛttiyuktaṃ kartavyaṃ yuṣmatprāṇopabṛṃhaṇam
english: Your purpose has been understood by me—it is the great welfare of the worlds; the duty bound up with active engagement is to be done, and it shall give increase to your very breath of life.

sanskrit: sutaptaṃ vas tapo devā mamārādhanakāmyayā bhokṣyathāsya mahāsattvās tapasaḥ phalam uttamam
english: Well practiced is your austerity, O gods, out of the desire to gratify me; you shall enjoy, O mighty beings, the supreme fruit of this penance.

sanskrit: eṣa brahmā lokaguruḥ sarvalokapitāmahaḥ yūyaṃ ca vibudhaśreṣṭhā māṃ yajadhvaṃ samāhitāḥ
english: This is Brahmā, the teacher of the worlds, the Grandfather of all the worlds; and you, O most excellent of the wise, worship me with collected minds.

sanskrit: sarve bhāgān kalpayadhvaṃ yajñeṣu mama nityaśaḥ tathā śreyo vidhāsyāmi yathādhīkāram īśvarāḥ
english: Apportion to me a share in your sacrifices, all of you, perpetually; thus shall I bestow well-being upon each according to his office, O lords.

sanskrit: śrutvaitad devadevasya vākyaṃ hṛṣṭatanūruhāḥ tatas te vibudhāḥ sarve brahmā te ca maharṣayaḥ
english: Hearing this utterance of the God of gods, the hair of their bodies bristling with joy, then all those wise ones, and Brahmā, and the great seers—

sanskrit: vedadṛṣṭena vidhinā vaiṣṇavaṃ kratum āharan tasmin satre tadā brahmā svayaṃ bhāgam akalpayat devā devarṣayaś caiva sarve bhāgān akalpayan
english: —by the rite seen in the Veda performed a sacrifice to Viṣṇu; at that session Brahmā himself apportioned a share, and the gods and divine seers all apportioned their shares.

sanskrit: te kārtayugadharmāṇo bhāgāḥ paramasatkṛtāḥ prāpur ādityavarṇaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ tamasaḥ param bṛhantaṃ sarvagaṃ devam īśānaṃ varadaṃ prabhum
english: Those shares, dharmic with the dharma of the Kṛta age and most reverently offered, reached that Person of the sun's own color, beyond darkness, the vast, all-pervading god, the sovereign, the boon-giving Lord.

sanskrit: tato 'tha varado devas tān sarvān amarān sthitān aśarīro babhāṣedaṃ vākyaṃ khastho maheśvaraḥ
english: Then the boon-giving god, the Great Lord, bodiless and abiding in the sky, spoke this utterance to all those immortals as they stood:

sanskrit: yena yaḥ kalpito bhāgaḥ sa tathā samupāgataḥ prīto 'haṃ pradiśāmy adya phalam āvṛttilakṣaṇam
english: "By whomsoever a share has been apportioned, even so has it duly come to me; pleased, I now grant the fruit that is marked by recurrence.

sanskrit: etad vo lakṣaṇaṃ devā matprasādasamudbhavam yūyaṃ yajñair ijyamānāḥ samāptavaradakṣiṇaiḥ yuge yuge bhaviṣyadhvaṃ pravṛttiphalabhoginaḥ
english: This is your mark, O gods, arising from my grace: being worshipped with sacrifices furnished with their full and blessed sacrificial fees, in age after age you shall be enjoyers of the fruit of active engagement.

sanskrit: yajñair ye cāpi yakṣyanti sarvalokeṣu vai surāḥ kalpayiṣyanti vo bhāgāṃs te narā vedakalpitān
english: And those men who shall sacrifice with sacrifices throughout all the worlds, O gods, they shall apportion to you your shares as ordained by the Veda.

sanskrit: yo me yathā kalpitavān bhāgam asmin mahākratau sa tathā yajñabhāgārho vedasūtre mayā kṛtaḥ
english: He who has apportioned to me his share in this great sacrifice—him, accordingly, have I made worthy of a sacrificial share in the canon of the Veda.

sanskrit: yūyaṃ lokān dhārayadhvaṃ yajñabhāgaphaloditāḥ sarvārthacintakā loke yathādhīkāranirmitāḥ
english: Sustain you the worlds, made to flourish by the fruit of your sacrificial shares, mindful of every purpose in the world, each fashioned according to his office.

sanskrit: yāḥ kriyāḥ pracariṣyanti pravṛttiphalasatkṛtāḥ tābhir āpyāyitabalā lokān vai dhārayiṣyatha
english: Whatever ritual acts shall be performed, hallowed with the fruit of active engagement, by these your strength shall be nourished, and so you shall sustain the worlds.

sanskrit: yūyaṃ hi bhāvitā loke sarvayajñeṣu mānavaiḥ māṃ tato bhāvayiṣyadhvam eṣā vo bhāvanā mama
english: For you shall be made to thrive in the world by men at all their sacrifices, and thereby you shall make me thrive in turn: this is my conception of you.

sanskrit: ityarthaṃ nirmitā vedā yajñāś cauṣadhibhiḥ saha ebhiḥ samyak prayuktair hi prīyante devatāḥ kṣitau
english: To this end were fashioned the Vedas, and the sacrifices together with their herbs; for by these rightly employed the deities upon the earth are gratified.

sanskrit: nirmāṇam etad yuṣmākaṃ pravṛttiguṇakalpitam mayā kṛtaṃ suraśreṣṭhā yāvat kalpakṣayād iti cintayadhvaṃ lokahitaṃ yathādhīkāram īśvarāḥ
english: This your making, fashioned of the quality of active engagement, has been wrought by me, O best of gods, to endure until the dissolution of the aeon; therefore take thought for the welfare of the worlds, each according to his office, O lords."

sanskrit: marīcir aṅgirāś cātriḥ pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ vasiṣṭha iti saptaite mānasā nirmitā hi vai
english: Marīci, Aṅgiras, and Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasiṣṭha—these seven were indeed fashioned from the mind.

sanskrit: ete vedavido mukhyā vedācāryāś ca kalpitāḥ pravṛttidharmiṇaś caiva prājāpatyena kalpitāḥ
english: These were appointed the foremost knowers of the Veda and the teachers of the Veda, and were ordained as followers of the dharma of active engagement by the lordship of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: ayaṃ kriyāvatāṃ panthā vyaktībhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ aniruddha iti prokto lokasargakaraḥ prabhuḥ
english: This is the eternal path of those given to ritual works, now made manifest; the Lord who is the maker of the creation of the worlds is called Aniruddha.

sanskrit: sanaḥ sanatsujātaś ca sanakaḥ sasanandanaḥ sanatkumāraḥ kapilaḥ saptamaś ca sanātanaḥ
english: Sana and Sanatsujāta, Sanaka and Sanandana, Sanatkumāra and Kapila, and the seventh, Sanātana—

sanskrit: saptaite mānasāḥ proktā ṛṣayo brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ svayamāgatavijñānā nivṛttaṃ dharmam āsthitāḥ
english: these seven are declared the mind-born seers, the sons of Brahmā, who attained knowledge of themselves and took their stand upon the dharma of withdrawal.

sanskrit: ete yogavido mukhyāḥ sāṃkhyadharmavidas tathā ācāryā mokṣaśāstre ca mokṣadharmapravartakāḥ
english: These are the foremost knowers of Yoga, knowers likewise of the dharma of Sāṃkhya, teachers in the science of liberation, and the promulgators of the dharma of liberation.

sanskrit: yato 'haṃ prasṛtaḥ pūrvam avyaktāt triguṇo mahān tasmāt parataro yo 'sau kṣetrajña iti kalpitaḥ so 'haṃ kriyāvatāṃ panthāḥ punarāvṛttidurlabhaḥ
english: From the Unmanifest, whence I first issued forth as the Great One of the three qualities—higher than that is He who is appointed the Knower of the Field; that very I am the path of those given to ritual works, hard to win without return again."

sanskrit: yo yathā nirmito jantur yasmin yasmiṃś ca karmaṇi pravṛttau vā nivṛttau vā tatphalaṃ so 'śnute 'vaśaḥ
english: As each creature has been fashioned, and for whatever work, whether in engagement or in withdrawal, the fruit of that he reaps, helpless to do otherwise.

sanskrit: eṣa lokagurur brahmā jagadādikaraḥ prabhuḥ eṣa mātā pitā caiva yuṣmākaṃ ca pitāmahaḥ mayānuśiṣṭo bhavitā sarvabhūtavarapradaḥ
english: "This is Brahmā, teacher of the worlds, the Lord who is the first maker of the universe; he is your mother and father, and your Grandfather too. Instructed by me, he shall become the bestower of boons upon all beings.

sanskrit: asya caivānujo rudro lalāṭād yaḥ samutthitaḥ brahmānuśiṣṭo bhavitā sarvatrasavarapradaḥ
english: And his younger brother Rudra, who arose from the forehead, instructed by Brahmā, shall become the bestower of boons upon all that moves.

sanskrit: gacchadhvaṃ svān adhīkārāṃś cintayadhvaṃ yathāvidhi pravartantāṃ kriyāḥ sarvāḥ sarvalokeṣu māciram
english: Go forth, take thought for your several offices as ordained; let all ritual acts proceed throughout all the worlds without delay.

sanskrit: pradṛśyantāṃ ca karmāṇi prāṇināṃ gatayas tathā parinirmitakālāni āyūṃṣi ca surottamāḥ
english: Let the works of living creatures be made manifest, and their destinies likewise, and their lifespans, whose seasons have been fully fashioned, O best of the gods.

sanskrit: idaṃ kṛtayugaṃ nāma kālaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ pravartate ahiṃsyā yajñapaśavo yuge 'smin naitad anyathā catuṣpāt sakalo dharmo bhaviṣyaty atra vai surāḥ
english: This age called the Kṛta, the most excellent of times, now sets in; in this age the sacrificial beasts are not to be slain—it shall be no otherwise—and here, O gods, dharma shall stand whole, upon all four feet.

sanskrit: tatas tretāyugaṃ nāma trayī yatra bhaviṣyati prokṣitā yatra paśavo vadhaṃ prāpsyanti vai makhe tatra pādacaturtho vai dharmasya na bhaviṣyati
english: Then comes the age called the Tretā, wherein the threefold Veda shall hold sway, and wherein the sprinkled beasts shall meet their slaughter at the rite; there a fourth part of dharma shall be no more.

sanskrit: tato vai dvāparaṃ nāma miśraḥ kālo bhaviṣyati dvipādahīno dharmaś ca yuge tasmin bhaviṣyati
english: Then comes the one called the Dvāpara, a mingled time, and in that age dharma shall be diminished by two feet.

sanskrit: tatas tiṣye 'tha saṃprāpte yuge kalipuraskṛte ekapādasthito dharmo yatra tatra bhaviṣyati
english: Then, when the Tiṣya age has come, ushered in by the Kali, dharma shall stand there upon a single foot."
